own_scenes.desc: La influencia directa de Kraftwerk sobre Afrika Bambaataa & the Soulsonic Force y el productor Arthur Baker dio «Planet Rock» (1982), que estalló en las pistas, definió el género electro (de «electronic funk») y cambió para siempre la manera de producir hip hop. Junto a Run-DMC y los Beastie Boys forma la combinación de rock y hip hop que luego la «electronica» explotaría.

notes.chapter: Cap. 3: Time to Express: Techno’s First Artists Emerge, 1981–1989
notes.text: «Planet Rock», hecha sobre la melodía de «Trans-Europe Express» y un ritmo como el de «Numbers», con la banda Planet Patrol, convirtió a Baker y Bambaataa en líderes del electro, que fue cosa de Nueva York (Newcleus, Mantronix) y de algún californiano (Egyptian Lover; Ice-T debutó en «Reckless», 1984); faltaba el Medio Oeste hasta Enter de Cybotron. Atkins estaba en Nueva York repartiendo cajas de «Cosmic Cars» el día que la radio estrenó «Planet Rock».

refs.q: The group’s direct influence on New York’s Afrika Bambaataa and the Soulsonic Force and producer Arthur Baker, for example, resulted in Bambaataa’s 1982 record “Planet Rock,” which exploded onto the dance scene and helped define the genre “electro” (short for “electronic funk”), changing forever the way hip-hop would be produced.
refs.para: The legacy of Kraftwerk’s sound can be neatly traced to many more recent forms of electronic music. The group’s direct influence on New York’s Afrika Bambaataa and the Soulsonic Force and producer Arthur Baker, for example, resulted in Bambaataa’s 1982 record “Planet Rock,” which exploded onto the dance scene and helped define the genre “electro” (short for “electronic funk”), changing forever the way hip-hop would be produced. But “Planet Rock” was only one single. Kraftwerk would also influence several other European and American sounds. Many Chicago house pioneers cite Kraftwerk’s 1981 record “Home Computer” as an early reference point. Likewise, electro and pre-techno artists in Detroit drew inspiration from the bizarre portamento riffs and lyrical minimalism of the group’s “Numbers,” also released in 1981.
refs.chapter: Cap. 1: Welcome to the Machine: America Wakes Up to Techno, 1997–2010

refs.q: Electro was one of the great dance music developments of the early 1980s that was neither a derivation nor an extension of disco.
refs.para: Fantasy’s interest in Cybotron coincided with the birth of a sound known as “electro,” presumably a shortening of “electronic funk.” Electro was one of the great dance music developments of the early 1980s that was neither a derivation nor an extension of disco. Instead, it was a “switched-on” funk variant, exaggerating the electronic sounds that Midwestern groups like Parliament-Funkadelic had perfected in the studio and brought onstage. Most critics point to New York, however, for the genre’s watershed moment.

podcast.title: Belgium Origin and Chemical Brothers Influence
podcast.body: A new electro sound emerged in Belgium, which found a very important base in The Chemical Brothers' pioneering work in blending electronic and rock elements. This sound gave rise to artists like Soulwax and 2manydjs. "una base muy importante para establecer el sonido el electro que se fundaría en Bélgica del que saldrían por ejemplo Soulwars to Menid DJs."

srcs.episode: The Chemical Brothers. Padres de la cultura BIG BEAT

podcast.title: Dance Sound in New York and Chicago
podcast.body: Electro was one of the various types of dance music that emerged from clubs in New York and Chicago, intriguing artists like New Order. It contributed to the evolving electronic sound that captivated the alternative dance scene. "And this is where they learned about post-disco, the growing house music movement, and various types of electro."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Foundation of Early Techno
podcast.body: The electro sound was central to early techno productions, notably "Alleys of Your Mind" by Cybotron, which laid the groundwork for the genre. "la cual, de su atener un sonido electro, sentó las bases del tecno."

srcs.episode: Cómo Detroit Reinventó la Música Electrónica ｜ Pioneros del Techno

podcast.title: Planet Rock as Foundational Track
podcast.body: Afrika Bambaataa's "Planet Rock," created by combining Kraftwerk melodies with a Roland TR-808, is recognized as the foundational track of the electro genre. "Planet Rock, el tema afundacional del electro, ya sabéis, uno de los pilares del gig-hop."

srcs.episode: Por qué KRAFTWERK es la banda más influyente de la historia?
